Step 7 – Critical current density Jc(T,B,θ) measurement  
Mount the bridge on a rotatable sample stage in a gas-He-flow cryostat (Janis Research) equipped with a 15-T cryogen-free magnet (JASTEC).  
- Temperature set-points: 65, 69, 73, 77.3, 81 K (Cernox thermometer beside sample).

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1: Target preparation  
- Two ceramic targets prepared by solid-state reaction: undoped YBCO and YBCO + 4 wt % BZO.  

Step 2: Film growth  
- Pulsed-laser deposition (PLD) on 10 mm × 10 mm SrTiO₃(100) substrates; film thickness ≈ 200 nm.  
- Exact PLD parameters are not listed; authors refer to earlier optimisation work.  

Step 3: Micro-bridge patterning (mask-less photolithography + wet etch)  
- Spin-coat Megaposit SPR 220-4.5 photoresist at 8000 rpm.  
- Expose pattern with Dilase 250 laser writer.  
- Develop in NaOH solution.  
- Etch unprotected YBCO in H₃PO₄ bath.  
- Strip resist in acetone.  
Final bridge: 50 µm wide, 2 mm long; contact pads for current and voltage as drawn in Fig. 1.  

Step 4: Resistor attachment for local heating  
- Glue a 220 Ω resistor (Loctite Stycast 2850FT) on the current pad ≈ 0.7 mm from the bridge; two Al wire-bonds connect it to the PPMS puck.  

Step 5: Electrical contacting  
- 33 µm Al wire-bonds (TPT HB05 bonder) link the sample to the PPMS puck: current leads at the two ends of the bridge, voltage taps in the middle.  

Step 6: Critical-current mapping  
- Measure I–V curves at every (T, B) point with PPMS AC transport option.  
- Define Ic with 1 µV cm⁻¹ electric-field criterion (bridge length 2 mm → 20 µV threshold).  

Step 7: MQE / quench search  
- Cool to 70 K; set magnetic field.  
- Apply a fixed transport current (expressed as %Ic).  
- Inject 0.7 s heat pulses by stepping the resistor current in 1 mA increments until a quench is detected (voltage jump ≈ 100 × noise).  
- Record the smallest resistor current that triggers a quench; compute MQE ≈ I²Rt with R = 220 Ω and t = 0.7 s.  
- Repeat for other %Ic, then change T or B; always increase absolute current as little as possible to postpone burnout.  

Step 8: NZPV extraction  
- Use voltage traces from the two farthest channels (3 and 4, 1 mm apart).  
- Measure time delay for each signal to cross a 10 mV threshold.  
- NZPV = 1 mm / Δt.  

Step 9: Post-mortem structural check  
- Cs-corrected STEM (JEOL JEM-2200FS, 200 kV, HAADF) on BZO-doped piece to image nanorods (diameter ≈ 6 nm, spacing ≈ 20 nm).  

[Experimental Design Details]
- Temperature range: 20 K – 70 K (PPMS variable-temperature insert).  
- Magnetic field: 0 – 8 T applied perpendicular to film plane (PPMS superconducting magnet).  
- Transport current limit: 1 A (PPMS maximum), corresponding to ≈ 10 MA cm⁻².  
- Heat-pulse duration: fixed at 0.7 s (not varied).  
- Voltage recording: National Instruments PXIe-1073 digitiser, LabVIEW control; four channels sampled simultaneously.  
- Samples eventually failed by burnout: APC-free at 30 K, 8 T, 0.9 Ic; BZO-doped at 30 K, 8 T, 0.5 Ic.

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1 – Substrate preparation  
- Start from commercial IBAD metal tapes (exact buffer stack not specified).  
- Deposit a 100–700 nm CeO₂ cap layer by RF magnetron sputtering to tailor surface texture.

Step 2 – Solution / dispersion preparation  
- Prepare FF-MOD coating solution: Gd, Ba, Cu precursors in fluorine-free solvents; total metal-ion concentration 0.6 mol L⁻¹.  
- Prepare separate BHO nanoparticle dispersion (particle size 1.6–2.2 nm by earlier DLS).  
- Mix the two to obtain precursor inks with 0–3.4 mol % BHO (most long-length work done at 2.7 mol %).

Step 3 – Coating & pyrolysis (repeated)  
- Slot-die coat the ink onto the CeO₂/IBAD tape.  
- Pyrolyse in 100 % O₂ from room temperature to 500 °C.  
- Repeat coating + pyrolysis 1–7 times until total REBCO thickness reaches 0.4–0.5 µm per cycle; final cumulative thickness 0.8–3.1 µm as required.

Step 4 – Crystallisation (reel-to-reel)  
- Heat pyrolysed film first at 700–840 °C in 100 ppm–100 % O₂ (1 atm total pressure) to decompose BaCO₃ and form polycrystalline GdBCO.  
- Cool to room temperature, then re-heat to 800–840 °C (same atmosphere) to obtain c-axis-oriented GdBCO with dispersed BHO.  
- The above two heating steps are collectively called “the crystallisation process” and are performed in a continuous reel-to-reel furnace.

Step 5 – Stabilisation / oxygenation  
- DC-sputter 100–700 nm Ag onto the superconducting film.  
- Oxygenate the tape at 200–500 °C in 100 % O₂.

Step 6 – Patterning for transport tests  
- Self-field Ic: chemically etch 1–2 mm-wide bridges.  
- In-field Ic (18 T): laser-pattern 80–85 µm-wide × 1 mm-long bridges.  
- Angular Ic (8 T): laser-pattern 0.5 mm-wide × 5 mm-long bridges.

Step 7 – Structural / microstructural characterisation  
- Measure in-plane texture (Δϕ) of CeO₂ and GdBCO by X-ray diffraction.  
- Observe surface morphology by SEM.  
- Acquire cross-sectional STEM images and map Hf by EDX to verify BHO dispersion (particles 2–10 nm after heat treatment).

Step 8 – Electrical measurements  
- Self-field Ic at 77 K: DC four-probe, 1 µV cm⁻¹ criterion.  
- In-field Ic up to 18 T at 20 K and 77 K: DC four-probe at HFLSM, Tohoku Univ.  
- Angular Ic at 20 K, fields ≤ 8 T: automated rotator (SuperCurrent system, RRI, NZ), 1 µV cm⁻¹ criterion.  
- Tc determination: four-probe R(T), define Tc as 90 % of normal-state resistance.  
- Long-length Ic uniformity: THEVA Tapestar mapping at 77.3 K under 80 mT (to avoid current limitation), 12 mm wide strip; values normalised to 4 mm width using a reference coupon measured by DC transport.

[Experimental Design Details]
- All process parameters (temperatures, O₂ partial pressure, number of coats, BHO content) are fixed for a given sample unless the text explicitly states otherwise.  
- Thickness control is achieved simply by counting coating–pyrolysis–crystallisation cycles; no in-situ thickness monitor is mentioned.  
- No details are given on heating/cooling rates, reel speed, or furnace residence time.  
- No information on precursor solvents, exact rare-earth salt types, or pH adjustment.  
- No post-annealing beyond the 200–500 °C oxygenation step is described.

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1: Substrate-decoration template preparation  
- Use polymer-assisted deposition (PAD, water-based metal-organic solution) to synthesise ZrO₂ nanoparticles  
- Deposit the solution onto (001) SrTiO₃ single-crystal substrates; anneal to obtain discrete ZrO₂ nano-islands  
- Store the decorated substrates for subsequent PLD growth  

Step 2: PLD target preparation  
- Fabricate a mixed ceramic ablation target containing YBCO plus 2.5 at % Ba₂YTaO₆ and 2.5 at % Ba₂YNbO₆ (total 5 at % BYNTO); detailed target manufacturing given in ref [38] of the paper  

Step 3: Film deposition  
- Mount either decorated (film A) or bare (film B) SrTiO₃ substrate on the PLD heater  
- Deposit YBCO-BYNTO layer by KrF excimer PLD: λ = 248 nm, 10 Hz, fluence ≈ 2 J cm⁻², substrate temperature 840 °C, growth rate ≈ 1.8 nm s⁻¹, final thickness ≈ 250 nm (measured 230 nm in micrographs)  
- Cool the sample; no post-annealing conditions are specified  

Step 4: Sample patterning for transport measurements  
- Cut 1 mm-long, 30–50 µm-wide bridges by standard photolithography and etching  

Step 5: Structural / morphological characterisation  
- AFM: image the decorated substrate before deposition to obtain nano-island diameter, height and density  
- X-ray diffraction: record ω-rocking curves of the (005) YBCO reflection with a 9 kW rotating-anode diffractometer in parallel-beam geometry  
- (S)TEM: prepare cross-sectional lamellae; acquire HAADF images and EDX maps to visualise nano-islands, nanocolumns, stacking faults, interface reactions  

Step 6: Electrical transport measurement  
- Load patterned bridges into a cryostat equipped with a superconducting magnet (maximum 18 T)  
- Apply magnetic field H || c-axis of YBCO (maximum Lorentz-force configuration)  
- Record current–voltage curves from 77 K down to 4.2 K in field steps; define Ic with 1 µV cm⁻¹ electric-field criterion  
- Compute Jc = Ic / cross-section and Fp = Jc µ₀H  

Step 7: Data analysis  
- Build Jc(H) curves at fixed temperatures  
- Evaluate irreversibility field µ₀Hirr from Fp(µ₀Hirr) = Fp_max/100  
- Construct normalised pinning-force curves f_p(h) = Fp(H)/Fp_max versus reduced field h = H/H_max (or H/Hirr) to test temperature scaling  
- Compare film A vs film B to isolate the effect of ZrO₂ nano-islands  

[Experimental Design Details]
Materials  
- Substrates: (001) SrTiO₃ single crystals, used as-received or after PAD decoration  
- Precursor solution for PAD: water-based metal-organic Zr salt plus polymer (exact chemistry not repeated here)  
- PLD target: YBCO + 2.5 at % Ba₂YTaO₆ + 2.5 at % Ba₂YNbO₆, mixed ceramic  

Key process parameters explicitly stated  
- PAD annealing: not detailed in this paper (referred to earlier works)  
- PLD: KrF 248 nm, 10 Hz, fluence ≈ 2 J cm⁻², T_sub = 840 °C, growth rate ≈ 1.8 nm s⁻¹, thickness ≈ 250 nm  

Structural metrics reported  
- Nano-island mean diameter 25 ± 9 nm, mean height 4.3 ± 0.9 nm, density ≈ 375 µm⁻², surface coverage ≈ 20 % (AFM, before deposition)  
- After growth some islands appear larger (~45–50 nm dia., ~25 nm height) due to BYNTO overgrowth  
- Stacking-fault density ~ 2 × 10⁴ µm⁻² (TEM, film A)  
- FWHM of (005) YBCO rocking curve 0.15° (film A) vs 0.24° (film B)  

Transport metrics  
- T_c: 83.7 K (film A) vs 87.2 K (film B)  
- Jc(0, 77 K): 1.0 MA cm⁻² (film A) vs 2.1 MA cm⁻² (film B)  
- µ₀Hirr(77 K): 4.6 T (film A) vs 5.1 T (film B)  
- Jc and Fp measured in 0–18 T, 4.2–77 K; full data tables and figures provided

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1 – Single-tape pre-characterisation  
- Measure Ic and n-value at 77 K, self-field, on the individual CFD and regular REBCO tapes intended for cabling (1 µV cm⁻¹ criterion).  

Step 2 – Bending-strain screening  
- Wind sample tapes (REBCO side facing former) on copper formers of decreasing diameter; record retained Ic after 45° bend.  
- Select the smallest former diameter that keeps Ic degradation ≤32 %; adopt 6.35 mm-OD copper rod + two heat-shrink layers → 6.9 mm bending diameter for cable winding.  

Step 3 – CFD tape preparation (reel-to-reel)  
- Mask 0.8 mm-wide stripes along both edges of 1 m-long SP REBCO tapes.  
- Chemically etch unmasked silver (aqueous H₂O₂:NH₄OH:H₂O 1:1:4) to create a high-resistivity degraded layer (Ri 100–320 µΩ cm²) under the future silver over-coat; remove mask; deposit silver.  
- Electroplate 10 µm Cu on 9–10 cm end sections (C1 & C3) to enable low-temperature indium soldering without Ag consumption.  
- Leave 50 cm sacrificial tail (C4) for winding grip; final usable length 30 cm.  

Step 4 – Regular tape preparation  
- Same length (1 m) and Cu-plated ends (D1 & D3) but no CFD patterning.  

Step 5 – CORC® cable winding  
- Wind two contra-helical layers (3 tapes each, 38.6° inner, 37.7° outer twist angle, 17 mm twist pitch) on the insulated 6.9 mm former; no inter-layer material added.  
- Cut sacrificial tails; obtain 30 cm active cable length.  
- Insert each cable end into a Cu tube (ID 9.4 mm, OD 12.7 mm); fill with indium solder to form 3 cm (regular) or 4 cm (CFD) termination.  

Step 6 – Room-temperature resistance check  
- Four-terminal measurement through termination voltage taps: 52 mΩ (CFD) and 44 mΩ (regular).  

Step 7 – Critical-current measurement  
- Immerse cable in liquid-N₂ (77 K) or in pumped-cryostat (65–77 K, ±0.05 K homogeneity).  
- Inject square current pulses (pulse width ≤ few 10 ms for NZPV, DC ramp for Ic).  
- Record total cable voltage; subtract terminal current-transfer component (baseline fit); apply 1 µV cm⁻¹ criterion to extract Ic and n-value.  
- Repeat for 67–77 K range on CFD cable; single-point calibration (76 K → 77 K, factor 1.15) used for regular cable.  

Step 8 – Normal-zone propagation velocity (NZPV) measurement  
- Mount 16 cm PCB equipped with spring-loaded pogo pins every 5.9 mm (one pin per outer-layer tape per twist pitch).  
- Place small NdFeB magnets under cable to create an 8 mm-long local Ic-depressed zone; trigger quench with a single current pulse.  
- Acquire pin voltages at ≥kHz sampling via multi-channel DAQ; define arrival time when local voltage reaches 0.1 V.  
- Compute NZPV = tap separation / time difference between successive taps; average left- and right-going fronts.  
- Sweep current 300–1200 A at 77 K; repeat in cryostat at 68.6, 71.3, 73.5, 77.3 K.  

Step 9 – Post-mortem inspection  
- Visually check for burn marks or degradation (regular cable failed at magnet location after 73.5 K run).

- Samples: 4 mm-wide SP REBCO tapes, 50 µm Hastelloy, 1.6 µm REBCO, 2.5 µm total Ag, no additional Cu stabiliser on cable section.  
- CFD zone: 3.2 mm width (f = 0.8), 26 cm length along each tape, Ri 100–320 µΩ cm².  
- Cable: 6 tapes, 2 layers, opposite twist, 30 cm active length, 6.9 mm final winding diameter.  
- Temperature: 65–77 K controlled by pumping on LN₂ bath; PT100 sensors at 4, 8, 12 cm heights.  
- Current: pulsed square wave (NZPV) or DC ramp (Ic); max ≈1.2 kA.  
- Electric-field criterion: 1 µV cm⁻¹ for Ic; 0.1 V for NZPV arrival time.  
- Voltage contacts: total cable taps for Ic; 5.9 mm-spaced pogo pins for NZPV.  
- Magnetic trigger: NdFeB cylinders, 8 mm influence length, placed inside sample-holder holes.

- Commercial oxide/carbonate powders (La₂O₃, Nd₂O₃, Eu₂O₃, Gd₂O₃, Y₂O₃, Er₂O₃, Yb₂O₃, BaCO₃, CuO; all ≥99.9 % purity) were weighed to give the atomic ratio RE : Ba : Cu = 1 : 2 : 3 for each of the five target compositions (Table 1).  

Step 2: Powder calcination (twice)  
- The mixed powders were heated in flowing air (200 SCCM) at 600 °C h⁻¹ to 940 °C, held 10 h, cooled at 60 °C h⁻¹ to 400 °C, then furnace-cooled to room temperature.  
- Manual grinding in an agate mortar for 15 min was carried out between the two identical calcination runs.  

Step 3: Bulk-sample forming  
- Calcined powder was uniaxially pressed in a 10 mm-inner-diameter cylindrical steel die at ≈250 MPa to form green pellets.  

Step 4: Bulk sintering  
- Pellets were sintered in flowing air at T = Tₚ + 5 °C (Tₚ individually measured by DSC) to generate a small liquid-phase assist.  
- After sintering, an oxygen-annealing step was added: 400 °C for 48 h in air (furnace cooled).  

Step 5: Phase identification & lattice-parameter determination  
- Room-temperature X-ray diffraction (Bruker D8 Advance, Cu Kα 40 kV/40 mA, 3 ° min⁻¹, 0.02 ° step) on powder samples; Rietveld refinement provided lattice parameters.  

Step 6: Thermal stability (Tₚ) measurement  
- DSC/TG (NETZSCH STA 449F5) on powders from 40 °C to 1100 °C at 5 °C min⁻¹ in flowing gas (air); Tₚ taken as the second endothermic peak (T₂).  

Step 7: Density measurement  
- Bulk density obtained by the Archimedes method; relative densities reported as 84–92 %.  

Step 8: Microstructural & compositional analyses  
- FE-SEM (JEOL JSM-IT800) with EDS on polished surfaces (successively ground to 2000-grit SiC, polished with 0.5 µm diamond paste, ultrasonically cleaned in alcohol; water contact minimized; final etch 0.5 wt % HCl in ethanol 4–6 s).

- Select next Ts–Y-ratio conditions either at the acquisition maximum, in unexplored regions, or at empirically promising points.

- Pattern films into 50–100 µm wide, 1 mm long bridges using a 355 nm UV laser marker.

- Perform standard DC four-probe I–V measurements in PPMS at 20 K (and additionally 77 K, 65 K) under magnetic fields up to 9 T.
